title: G4: Degree bound of F independent of n (the binding constraint)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (uniform degree).** The coordinate functions of $\mathbf{F}$ must have degrees bounded by an absolute constant, independent of $n$; only the number $N$ of coordinates may grow with $n$.

The prior docs invoke Hochster–Huneke ('toric ideal generated in degree $\le$ dimension'), but the dimension here grows with $n$, so this yields an **$n$-dependent** bound and does NOT establish property (2). One needs a genuine local-to-global rigidity: a generating family in which each relation involves only a constant number of tuples (hence constant degree). This is the property that makes the problem interesting and is the main thing a correct proof must deliver (corresponds to P4).

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Resolved.** The current solution already meets the binding constraint (degree of F independent of n), and crucially does so **without** the flawed Hochster–Huneke route. I verified this in detail and added an explicit remark (Remark "Uniform degree and local rigidity") isolating the two quantitative features the issue demands.

**What delivers property (2):** F is the tuple of all 5x5 minors of the four mode-flattenings S_(m) of the assembled tensor S. Each coordinate of F is therefore a polynomial of degree **exactly 5**, an absolute constant. Only the *number* N of coordinates grows with n; the *degrees* do not. The threshold value 4 (rank <= 4) is intrinsic to the single shared factor A^(alpha) in R^{3x4} of width 4 in the Levi-Civita unfolding (eq. hfactor), independent of n. No degree=dimension generation statement (Hochster-Huneke) is used anywhere.

**Genuine local-to-global rigidity (the P4 point):** The converse lower bound r_off >= 2 ==> rank(S_(m)) >= 5 (Theorem thm:lower) is *local*: its proof produces 5 independent columns inside a single 6x27 submatrix determined by exactly **two row blocks a1,a2 and two ordinary triples c,c'** -- i.e. only four of the input tensors. So a violated rank-one condition is always witnessed by a bounded-degree relation among a bounded (n-independent) number of tuples. Patching these constant-arity certificates over all index choices gives the global characterization. This is exactly the local rigidity the issue asked for, in place of an n-dependent toric bound.

**Numerical confirmation (workspace checks):**
- rank-one off-diagonal lambda ==> rank(S_(m)) = 4 for all modes (n=5).
- generic off-diagonal lambda ==> rank = 15 = 3n for all modes (n=5).
- exact identity rank(S_(m)) = min(4*r_m^off, 3n): a mode-1-rank-2 lambda gives rank 8 = min(8,18) in mode 1 (n=6), >=5 as required.
- Step C of Theorem thm:lower (dim(W+EW) >= 5 whenever p!=q under generic kernel conditions) verified over 2000 random trials.

The degree bound is therefore established rigorously and n-uniformly. Closing as resolved.
